chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the rights of the guest is that he should be honoured, and that the toothpick be prepared for him'.

key_terms.الْخِلَالُ: Toothpick (used for cleaning teeth, symbolizing care)

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a guest in Shia Islam according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Prophetic tradition of hospitality, linking the physical care of the guest—symbolized by preparing the *khilal* (toothpick)—to the broader ethical obligation of *ikram* (honouring). In Shia scholarly tradition, this specific detail highlights that true generosity extends to minute details of comfort, reflecting the high status of the guest as a trust from God. It serves as a practical guideline for Muslims to embody benevolence in daily social interactions.
